pr_body:
# Objective

Fix https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/4530

- Make it easier to open/close/modify windows by setting them up as `Entity`s with a `Window` component.
- Make multiple windows very simple to set up. (just add a `Window` component to an entity and it should open)

## Solution

- Move all properties of window descriptor to ~components~ a component.
- Replace `WindowId` with `Entity`.
- ~Use change detection for components to update backend rather than events/commands. (The `CursorMoved`/`WindowResized`/... events are kept for user convenience.~
  Check each field individually to see what we need to update, events are still kept for user convenience.

---

## Changelog

- `WindowDescriptor` renamed to `Window`.
    - Width/height consolidated into a `WindowResolution` component.
    - Requesting maximization/minimization is done on the [`Window::state`] field.
- `WindowId` is now `Entity`.

## Migration Guide

- Replace `WindowDescriptor` with `Window`.
    - Change `width` and `height` fields in a `WindowResolution`, either by doing
      ```rust
      WindowResolution::new(width, height) // Explicitly
      // or using From<_> for tuples for convenience
      (1920., 1080.).into()
      ```
- Replace any `WindowCommand` code to just modify the `Window`'s fields directly  and creating/closing windows is now by spawning/despawning an entity with a `Window` component like so:
  ```rust
  let window = commands.spawn(Window { ... }).id(); // open window
  commands.entity(window).despawn(); // close window
  ```

## Unresolved
- ~How do we tell when a window is minimized by a user?~
  ~Currently using the `Resize(0, 0)` as an indicator of minimization.~
  No longer attempting to tell given how finnicky this was across platforms, now the user can only request that a window be maximized/minimized.
  
 ## Future work
 - Move `exit_on_close` functionality out from windowing and into app(?)
 - https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/5621
 - https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/7099
 - https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/7098

@tigregalis I think it might make sense to maybe remove `ClearColor` as a resource given the changes to camera-driven rendering. You should be able to have different clear colors per window by using a different `Camera` per window with a different clear color for each.

> Lots of small bits of feedback. Generally strongly in favor of this design.
> 
> Feeling very iffy about the `InitialWindow` design though: it definitely feels like something that should be recorded using a marker component. IMO we should spawn the initial window entity manually (directly on the world), even before startup systems run, in order to bypass the need for a special cased resource.

We already spawn the entity directly with the plugin I believe, so we could just modify it to use a marker component instead of a resource.
Yes please, that would feel much more natural to me.

I'm not sure how viable it is to have this `WindowState` enum, it seems way too easy to have it desync from the state of the window, not to mention it is extremely subjective what is "minimized"/"maximized"/"normal"/etc.
I'm going to make it more of a "write only" struct where you can request that the window be minimized/maximized.

I'm going to do 1 more quick pass through myself tomorrow, but I think this is ready for merging. @alice-i-cecile the only thing I didn't really change based on reviews was the wasm stuff here (reasoning for why is there as well):
https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/5589#discussion_r103537753
Refactored it into a singular component, should be more ready now

Just pushed some changes (all negotiable / easily revertible via separate commits):
* **Simplified multiple windows example**: this isn't a "minimizing" example. i don't think its worth complicating this with extra windows + config
* **Flattened out the canvas fields**: The canvas wrapper type introduced unnecessary complexity / naming confusion (ex: `canvas.cavas`)
* **Combined cursor type fields**: The `Cursor` type didn't include the cursor_position, which felt odd
* **Removed WindowState**: I added a new "InternalWindowState" that holds anything that should be abstracted away from the user. I also removed the attempts at exposing the "maximized" state, as the approach used is loss-ey (user-triggered maximize / minimize events are not represented). If we want to add support for this, we should resolve this. Which can be done in a separate PR.
* **Used simpler Window queries in examples**: This will be controversial, but I don't think filtering for PrimaryWindow is justified complexity for 99.9% of games/apps (which will be single-windowed). `Query<&Windows>` is simpler / easier. And we are already using `windows.single()`, which will fail in the event that there is more than one window. This is pretty much as safe as the `With<PrimaryWindow>` filter. Biggest difference is that we will panic in these cases instead of continuing to work. This _is_ a loss, but imo an acceptable one when considered globally.

issue_context.title: Windows as entities
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

Windows can't be closed from within bevy, #3575 mentions windows as entities and i really like that idea of that, so here is a proposal on how it could be done

## What solution would you like?

`WindowId` is now `Entity`

Extend `Commands` with a `window` method returns `WindowCommands` similar to how the `entity` method returns `EntityCommands`, `WindowCommandQueued` will implement `Command` and on `write` send itself as an event that window backends like `bevy_winit` will process.

`Window` should be separated into different components, `WindowCursor`, `WindowCursorPosition`, `WindowHandle`, `WindowPosition`, `WindowResizeConstraints`, `WindowResolution`, `WindowTitle`, as well as these markers `WindowCurrentlyFocused` (`WindowFocused` is taken by a window event), `WindowDecorated`, `WindowResizable`. 
A world query struct containing all these components and markers should be publicly exposed..

Windows should be spawned like an entity in `Commands` with a `WindowDescriptor` component, window backends should query `Added<WindowDescriptor>` and create the windows for them, while also applying a `Window` marker confirming they have been created, query `Added<Window>` or use a `WindowCreated` event to get newly created windows.

Despawning windows should be done just as entities (as they are now entities), window backends should close/destroy windows their internal component has been dropped, e.g. `WinitWindow` (wrapper around winit's `Window` that destroys itself on drop)

A resource called `PrimaryWindow` contains the entity id of initial window created by `WindowPlugin`, this replaces Windows::primary

`WindowPlugin` should change `exit_on_close` into a enum called `ExitCondition` with the values `OnPrimaryClosed` (when primary window is closed), `OnAllClosed` (when all windows are closed), `DontExit` (keep app headless)
